question.text: A point is in motion along a hyperbola $y=\frac{10}{x}$ so that its abscissa $x$ increases uniformly at a rate of 1 unit per second. Then, the rate of change of its ordinate when the point passes through (5,2)

options.text: increases at the rate of $\frac{1}{2}$ unit per second
decreases at the rate of $\frac{1}{2}$ unit per second
decreases at the rate of $\frac{2}{5}$ unit per second
increases at the rate of $\frac{2}{5}$ unit per second

solution.text:
We have,
$$
\begin{array}{r}
\frac{d x}{d t}=\operatorname{l and} y=\frac{10}{x} \\
\text { Now, } y=\frac{10}{x}
\end{array}
$$
On differentiating both the sides w.r.t. $t$, we get
$$
\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d t} &=\frac{-10}{x^{2}} \times \frac{d x}{d t} \\
&=\frac{-10}{(5)^{2}} \times 1
\end{aligned}
$$
$$
=\frac{-10}{25}=\frac{-2}{5} \quad\left[x=5, \frac{d x}{d t}=1\right]
$$
$\therefore y$ decreases at the rate of $\frac{2}{5}$ unit per second.
